title: A2 Writing Quiz 9 — Friends, Family & Celebrations

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Have you ever organized a birthday party?
Have you ever organize a birthday party?
Did you ever organized a birthday party?
Have you ever organizes a birthday party?
questions.explanation: Present perfect question: Have + subject + past participle: 'Have you ever organized a birthday party?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We have celebrated my sister's wedding last summer.
We celebrated my sister's wedding last summer.
We have celebrate my sister's wedding last summer.
We are celebrating my sister's wedding last summer.
questions.explanation: A finished time expression ('last summer') needs past simple, not present perfect.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We were dancing when the lights suddenly went out.
We danced when the lights were suddenly going out.
We were dance when the lights suddenly went out.
We dancing were when the lights suddenly went out.
questions.explanation: Past continuous (background) + past simple (interruption): 'We were dancing when the lights went out.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: My cousin is friendlier than my neighbour.
My cousin is more friendly than my neighbour.
My cousin is friendliest than my neighbour.
My cousin is friendly than my neighbour.
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -y change to -ier: 'friendlier than'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This was the happiest day of my life.
This was the more happy day of my life.
This was the most happiest day of my life.
This was happiest day of my life.
questions.explanation: Adjectives ending in -y change to -iest for superlatives: 'the happiest day'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Can I invite my cousin to the party?
Can I inviting my cousin to the party?
Can I to invite my cousin to the party?
I can invite my cousin to the party can?
questions.explanation: 'Can' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'Can I invite...?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: You should bring a gift to the wedding.
You should to bring a gift to the wedding.
You should bringing a gift to the wedding.
You should brings a gift to the wedding.
questions.explanation: 'Should' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'should bring'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Would you like coming to my birthday party?
Would you like to come to my birthday party?
Would you like come to my birthday party?
Would you liked to come to my birthday party?
questions.explanation: 'Would like' is followed by the infinitive with 'to': 'would like to come'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We're going to celebrate Grandma's birthday this Sunday.
We're going celebrate Grandma's birthday this Sunday.
We going to celebrate Grandma's birthday this Sunday.
We're going to celebrating Grandma's birthday this Sunday.
questions.explanation: 'Going to' + base verb expresses a plan: 'going to celebrate'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If you come to the party, you will meet my cousins.
If you will come to the party, you meet my cousins.
If you come to the party, you meet will my cousins.
If you came to the party, you will meet my cousins.
questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb: 'If you come..., you will meet...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I enjoy spending time with my family on weekends.
I enjoy to spend time with my family on weekends.
I enjoy spend time with my family on weekends.
I enjoy spent time with my family on weekends.
questions.explanation: 'Enjoy' is followed by a gerund (-ing form): 'enjoy spending'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We decided having a small family gathering.
We decided to have a small family gathering.
We decided have a small family gathering.
We decided for have a small family gathering.
questions.explanation: 'Decide' is followed by the infinitive with 'to': 'decided to have'.

questions.question: There weren't ___ guests at the small dinner party.
options: much
many
a little
much of
questions.explanation: 'Guests' is countable and plural, so 'many' is used in negative sentences.

questions.question: We only invited ___ close friends to the dinner.
options: a little
a few
much
little
questions.explanation: 'Friends' is countable, and 'a few' means 'a small number of'.

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses 'especially'.
options: Everyone enjoyed the party, especially the children.
Everyone enjoyed the party, especially but the children.
Especially everyone enjoyed the party the children.
Everyone enjoyed the party especially, the children.
questions.explanation: 'Especially' highlights a specific example: 'the party, especially the children.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We arrived early so that we could help set up.
We arrived early so that could we help set up.
We arrived early for so we could help set up.
We arrived early so that helping set up.
questions.explanation: 'So that' + clause expresses purpose: 'so that we could help set up.'

questions.question: We organized a dinner ___ our grandmother's birthday.
options: in honour of
for honour of
on honour
at honour of
questions.explanation: 'In honour of' + noun means 'to celebrate or respect someone': 'in honour of her birthday.'

questions.question: ___ my brother, everyone came to the reunion.
options: Apart from
Except of
Besides of
Away from
questions.explanation: 'Apart from' + noun means 'except for': 'Apart from my brother, everyone came.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "I miss my grandparents.")
options: She said that she misses her grandparents.
She said that she missed her grandparents.
She said that she is missing her grandparents.
She said she miss her grandparents.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, present simple usually shifts to past simple: 'she missed her grandparents.'

questions.question: Which is the correct way to start an email to a cousin inviting them to a family gathering?
options: Dear Sir/Madam,
Hi Leyla,
To Whom It May Concern,
Dear Customer,
questions.explanation: 'Hi [Name],' is a friendly, informal greeting suitable for a family member.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to end a warm email to a family member?
options: Yours faithfully,
Love,
Sincerely,
Regards,
questions.explanation: 'Love,' is a warm, informal closing suitable for close family and friends.

questions.question: Choose the correct suggestion.
options: Let's plan a surprise party for Dad.
Let's to plan a surprise party for Dad.
Let's planning a surprise party for Dad.
Let's planned a surprise party for Dad.
questions.explanation: 'Let's' + base verb is used to make a suggestion: 'Let's plan a surprise party...'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly combines 'This is my aunt.' and 'My aunt taught me how to cook.'?
options: This is my aunt which taught me how to cook.
This is my aunt who taught me how to cook.
This is my aunt what taught me how to cook.
This is my aunt taught me who to cook.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is used for people in relative clauses: 'my aunt who taught me how to cook.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We usually visit our grandparents on Sundays.
We visit usually our grandparents on Sundays.
Usually we visit our grandparents on Sundays always.
We visit our grandparents usually on Sundays.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of frequency usually go before the main verb: 'We usually visit our grandparents.'

questions.question: Which sentence has correct punctuation?
options: Do you know what time the party starts?
Do you know what time does the party start?
Do you know what time the party starts.
Do you know, what time the party starts?
questions.explanation: Indirect questions keep normal word order and end with a question mark: 'what time the party starts?'

questions.question: We ___ this celebration for weeks, so everything should go smoothly.
options: plan
have planned
have been planning
planned
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous emphasizes duration of an ongoing action: 'have been planning'.

questions.question: This gift isn't mine, it's ___.
options: he
him
his
his's
questions.explanation: Possessive pronoun (stands alone, no noun after it): 'it's his.'

questions.question: Choose the sentence that correctly uses sequencing words.
options: First, decorate the hall. Next, prepare the food. Finally, welcome the guests.
First decorate hall next prepare food finally welcome guests.
Finally decorate the hall, first prepare food, next welcome guests.
Next first decorate hall, finally prepare welcome guests.
questions.explanation: Sequencing words 'First,', 'Next,' and 'Finally,' organize steps clearly with commas.

questions.question: Every guest at the wedding ___ a small gift bag.
options: receive
receives
receiving
are receiving
questions.explanation: 'Every' takes a singular verb: 'Every guest receives...'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You've met my cousin before, haven't you?
You've met my cousin before, have you?
You've met my cousin before, didn't you?
You've met my cousin before, haven't?
questions.explanation: Positive statement + negative tag: 'You've met my cousin before, haven't you?'
